HIST.01.note: Australian Geographic places the 1932 military cull within soldier-settlement farming, drought, crop damage and later wildlife-management policy, correcting the meme that Australia formally declared a conventional war.

exercise.prompt: Rewrite the Emu War as a policy case study with stakeholders, ecological causes, military objectives, measured outcomes, media framing and the later fence-and-bounty alternatives.

HIST.02.note: Smithsonian's account follows pepper and other Asian spices through Venice, Portuguese ocean routes and Dutch monopoly power while rejecting the myth that spices mainly disguised rotten meat.

exercise.prompt: Trace one spice from growing region to European table across producers, regional traders, ports, empires, monopolies and consumers, marking where value and coercive power accumulated.

HIST.03.note: The Library of Congress guide separates documented Gutenberg history from legend and explicitly notes that printing began in East Asia centuries before European movable-metal-type printing.

article.title: The Gutenberg Bible at the Library of Congress: Introduction

exercise.prompt: Compare manuscript copying, woodblock printing and movable type by setup cost, marginal copy cost, error correction, labour, speed, scale, censorship and access.

HIST.04.note: The debunk focuses on the hypothesis's calendar mistake and the independent chronologies supplied by tree rings, radiocarbon dating, astronomical observations and non-European records.

article.title: Phantom Time Hypothesis — the Supposedly ‘Missing’ Fortnight in 1752

exercise.prompt: Build an independent-evidence matrix for the disputed centuries using European documents, Islamic and Chinese chronology, eclipses, comets, dendrochronology, radiocarbon and archaeology.

HIST.05.note: Eric Cline's overview rejects a single-cause invasion story and presents the collapse as a connected-system failure involving warfare, migration, political unrest, disrupted trade, earthquakes and climate stress.

article.title: Interview: The Mysterious Bronze Age Collapse with Eric Cline
article.source: World History Encyclopedia — Eric H. Cline

exercise.prompt: Draw the Late Bronze Age eastern Mediterranean as a network of palaces, trade, food, metals and security, then model how several smaller shocks could cascade through it.

HIST.06.note: The National Archaeological Museum's dedicated project presents the fragments, inscriptions, imaging research and reconstructed astronomical functions without calling the device a modern digital computer.

article.title: The Mysteries of the Mechanism of Antikythera

exercise.prompt: Choose one dial and reconstruct the required input, gear ratio, output cycle and astronomical purpose, distinguishing evidence on fragments from modern reconstruction.

HIST.07.note: The Open University compares the sparse ancient and much later accounts and shows why Caesar, the Serapeum and the Arab-conquest story cannot be merged into one cinematic destruction event.

article.title: The Library of Alexandria — The Destruction of the Library

exercise.prompt: Create a source timeline for Caesar's fire, later Roman decline, the Serapeum destruction and the Arab-conquest legend, recording source dates and what each actually claims.

HIST.08.note: The museum history integrates fission science, dispersed industrial sites, military organization, secrecy, uranium and plutonium production, bomb design and the continuing ethical and environmental legacy.

article.title: The Manhattan Project
article.source: National Museum of Nuclear Science & History / Atomic Heritage Foundation

exercise.prompt: Map Los Alamos, Oak Ridge, Hanford, Chicago and military command by scientific task, industrial bottleneck, workforce, secrecy requirement, hazard and ethical decision.

HIST.09.note: The historical article reconstructs how contemporaries interpreted the Strasbourg outbreak through disease, divine punishment and social conditions; mass psychogenic illness is a serious proposal, not a proved diagnosis.

article.title: Divine Punishment or Disease? Medieval and Early Modern Approaches to the 1518 Strasbourg Dancing Plague
article.source: Lynneth J. Miller — Dance and History bibliography

exercise.prompt: Compare ergot poisoning, deliberate ritual, neurological disease and mass psychogenic illness by expected symptoms, spread, contemporary evidence and weaknesses.

HIST.10.note: The Nuclear Museum traces radium-dial production, corporate denial, bone damage, litigation and the workers' influence on radiation protection and occupational safety.

article.title: The Radium Girls
article.source: National Museum of Nuclear Science & History / Atomic Heritage Foundation

exercise.prompt: Build a failure chain from brush practice through internal exposure, delayed symptoms, company knowledge, medical evidence, legal barriers, compensation and later safety standards.

HIST.11.note: Boston's official centenary account uses city-archive photographs and emphasizes the untested tank, victims, litigation and resulting movement toward professional engineering oversight.

article.title: 100 Years Ago Today: Molasses Crashes Through Boston’s North End

exercise.prompt: Perform a modern hazard review of the tank covering design pressure, material, foundation, temperature, filling rate, inspection, warning signs, emergency planning and regulatory approval.

HIST.12.note: The Open Encyclopedia of Anthropology explains that 'cargo cult' bundled diverse Melanesian religious and political movements into a colonial academic category, often obscuring local critiques of unequal exchange and power.

article.title: Cargo Cults
article.source: Open Encyclopedia of Anthropology — Lamont Lindstrom

exercise.prompt: Take one named Melanesian movement and describe its colonial setting, theology, leadership, political demands and local meaning before judging whether the label cargo cult clarifies or distorts it.
